newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB keeps discount rate at 1.00 pct after meeting.
newsitem.headline: SNB keeps discount rate at 1.00 pct after meeting.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) left its discount rate unchanged at 1.00 percent after a regular weekly meeting of its three-man policy-setting board.
The SNB last changed the discount rate when it was lowered to 1.00 percent from 1.50 percent on September 26.
"No change," an SNB spokesman said in response to an enquiry after the meeting had ended.
No changes in the rate were expected at today's meeting.
The Swiss economy remains in the doldrums, according to data released on Thursday.
Swiss unemployment hit a post-World War Two high of 5.3 percent in December, according to data released by the Federal Office of Trade, Industry and Labour.
In addition, on Thursday the Swiss Federal Statistics Office said domestic retail sales fell 0.8 percent in November.

The Swiss Centre for Research of Economic Activity (KOF) also said Thursday that its economic barometer rose by only 0.1 percent in November, and that it expected the economy to remain slack in the first few months of 1997.
